purpose: Delta gate for agent skill packages: block a skill when its security posture changes, not when it merely matches a pattern.
rationale: Absolute gating on a high-recall/low-precision scanner forces whole-skill bypasses, which are permanent holes. Approving a package at a reviewed state and blocking only on NEW findings makes constant scanner noise harmless and makes any change to a trusted external skill an explicit review event.

optional_llm.note: Bring your own key. Adds semantic analysis; not load-bearing. Set SKILL_SCANNER_LLM_{PROVIDER,BASE_URL,API_KEY,MODEL}.

fail_closed_note: An unscannable or SKILL.md-less package is never approved.

hash_exclusions.rationale: Some skills legitimately write runtime state into their own installed directory (daily-cleanup-triage writes logs/ and __pycache__). Hashing those would make the content tripwire churn on every run. Such paths are EXCLUDED FROM THE HASH BUT STILL SCANNED, so a payload dropped into a runtime directory is still blocked. NOTHING is excluded by default: a package earns an exclusion only by declaring the path in its own .gitignore AND that name appearing in `paths` below. Granting this list unconditionally let any package that shipped no .gitignore hide a directory named logs/ or node_modules/ from the tripwire for free.
hash_exclusions.nestable_rationale: Names that legitimately appear below the package root. Everything else is root-anchored: declaring `logs` must not also exclude `scripts/logs/`, which would be a hiding place one directory deeper than the package declared.

invisible_character_policy.rationale: Invisible and direction-controlling codepoints are never legitimate in a skill package. They are invisible to a human reviewer AND to an LLM analyser, which makes them the highest-leverage place to hide an instruction or to split a keyword so literal matching fails. This class must be caught deterministically; it cannot be delegated to a semantic analyser.
